name: โรคข้ออักเสบปฏิกิริยา
pinyin: fǎn yìng xìng guān jié yán
preview_text: ข้อต่อที่ร้อนและบวมซึ่งรู้สึกดีขึ้นเมื่อสัมผัสกับน้ำแข็งและความเย็น ข้อต่อที่ปวดเมื่อยและต้องการแผ่นทำความร้อนนั้นไม่ใช่โรคข้ออักเสบแบบเดียวกัน - TCM ปฏิบัติต่อแต่ละข้อด้วยข้อที่แตกต่างกันโดยสิ้นเชิง
categories: ["เงื่อนไขข้อและข้ออักเสบ"]
conventional_description: Reactive arthritis is a form of inflammatory arthritis that develops in response to an infection elsewhere in the body, most often in the gut or urinary tract. The immune system, triggered by the infection, mistakenly attacks the joints, causing pain, swelling, and stiffness - typically in the knees, ankles, and feet. It can also affect the eyes, skin, and urinary tract. Diagnosis is based on your symptoms and a history of recent infection, as there is no single lab test for it. The condition is often self-limiting, resolving within a few months, but some people experience recurrent flares or chronic arthritis.
conventional_treatments: Conventional treatment focuses on reducing inflammation and managing symptoms. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen are usually first-line. If NSAIDs aren't enough, corticosteroid injections or oral steroids may be used to quickly calm a flare. For persistent or severe cases, disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) such as sulfasalazine or methotrexate can be prescribed to suppress the overactive immune response. Physical therapy helps maintain joint mobility and strength.
tcm_understanding:
TCM understands reactive arthritis as a form of 'Bi syndrome' (Painful Obstruction), where external pathogenic factors invade the body's channels and joints after a gut or urinary infection has weakened your defensive Qi. The infection leaves behind a lingering pathogen - often Dampness combined with Heat or Cold - that travels through the body and settles in the joints, blocking the flow of Qi and Blood. This obstruction is what causes the pain, swelling, and stiffness.
Which pathogen dominates depends on your constitution and the nature of the original infection. If you tend toward heat signs and the infection was acute with fever, Damp-Heat may lodge in your joints, making them red, hot, and intensely painful. If you are more prone to cold and the illness was slow and lingering, Cold-Damp may invade, causing a deep, aching pain that worsens in chilly, damp weather. Sometimes the pathogen is purely Dampness, leading to heavy, swollen joints and a sense of fatigue.
Over time, if the obstruction is not cleared, it can damage the channels further and deplete your body's deeper reserves. Blood Stagnation may develop, causing fixed, stabbing pain that is worse at night. The Liver and Kidneys, which nourish the sinews and bones, can become deficient, leading to chronic, dull aches and weakness. Even your Qi and Yin can be depleted after a prolonged illness, leaving you with lingering joint pain, profound fatigue, and a dry mouth.
This is why TCM doesn't have a single treatment for reactive arthritis. The red, hot joint after a urinary infection and the cold, aching joint that flares in winter are two different diseases in TCM terms. Your practitioner will look at your tongue, feel your pulse, and ask about what makes your pain better or worse to identify your unique pattern, then choose herbs and acupuncture points that specifically address it.
classical_quote: 「风寒湿三气杂至，合而为痹也。」
classical_translation: "The three Qi of wind, cold, and dampness arrive together, and combine to form Bi (painful obstruction)."

tcm_diagnosis:
When reactive arthritis flares suddenly after an infection, a TCM practitioner looks for signs of Damp Heat invading the channels. The affected joints feel hot to the touch, look red, and are intensely swollen and painful. The person may also feel feverish and thirsty. The tongue appears red with a thick yellow greasy coating, and the pulse is rapid and slippery. This picture points clearly to the Damp Heat pattern, the most common acute presentation.
If the joints ache with a cold, heavy sensation and pain worsens in cold or damp weather, the pattern shifts toward Wind-Cold-Damp. The skin over the joints is not red or hot; instead, the person feels chilled and prefers warmth. The tongue is pale and puffy with a white greasy coat, while the pulse feels tight, like a taut string. This pattern often arises when the original infection involved more Cold than Heat.
In some cases, the dominant pathogen is Dampness rather than Heat or Cold. The joints feel heavy and swollen, and the pain is fixed and aching rather than sharp or burning. The person may complain of numbness in the limbs and a sensation of being weighed down. Dampness also affects the Spleen, leading to poor appetite, bloating, and loose stools. The tongue is pale and swollen with a thick, greasy white coating, and the pulse is soggy and slow. This pattern often lingers and can combine with Cold or Heat over time.
As reactive arthritis persists, Blood Stagnation can develop, especially if the pain becomes fixed and stabbing, like a knife, rather than moving. The pain often intensifies at night. The tongue may appear dark purple or show distinct purple spots, and the pulse feels rough or choppy. A practitioner will ask about the exact nature of the pain and any history of trauma to confirm this less common but important pattern.
In chronic or recurrent cases, underlying weakness in the Liver and Kidney systems becomes evident. The person complains of a dull, aching pain in the lower back and knees, along with pronounced fatigue and weakness. The tongue is pale with a thin coat, and the pulse is thin and weak. A long history of joint problems, aging, or overwork points toward this deficiency pattern, which often underlies the more acute flare-ups.
Prolonged inflammation or medication use can deplete Qi and Yin, leading to joint pain accompanied by deep fatigue, dry mouth, and a sensation of heat in the palms or soles. The tongue looks red with little or no coating, sometimes with cracks, and the pulse is thready and rapid. This pattern is seen in long-standing cases where the body’s nourishing fluids have been consumed, requiring a different treatment approach than acute damp-heat.

patterns.pattern_name: Painful Obstruction due to Damp Heat in Channels
patterns.symptoms: ["Joints are red, hot, and swollen", "Pain eased by cold, worsened by warmth", "Heavy, aching sensation in limbs", "Fever or feeling of body heat", "Irritability and restlessness", "Dark, scanty urine"]
patterns.worse_with: Hot weather or heat, Spicy, greasy food, Alcohol, Overexertion or overwork, Emotional stress
patterns.better_with: Cold compresses, Rest, Cool environment, Light, non-greasy foods, Drinking plenty of water
patterns.why_this_happens: Reactive arthritis often begins after a gut or urinary infection. In TCM, the infection leaves behind Damp-Heat that hasn't been completely cleared. This Damp-Heat travels through the body and settles in the joints, blocking the flow of Qi and blood. The trapped Dampness causes swelling and heaviness, while the Heat creates redness and intense burning pain, producing the classic angry, inflamed joints.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body, slightly swollen, with a yellow greasy coating. Pulse: slippery and rapid, may feel soggy or wiry at the Guan position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold compresses and a cool environment directly counteract the internal Heat that causes redness and burning pain. Rest prevents further strain on the already inflamed channels. Spicy, greasy foods and alcohol add more Damp-Heat to the body, making joint swelling and heat worse. Overexertion and stress stir up Qi and generate more internal Heat, so calming down and pacing activity are essential.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods, as well as alcohol, which all generate damp-heat. Choose cooling, light foods like mung beans, cucumber, watermelon, and barley. During acute flares, apply cold compresses to the joints and rest, but once the inflammation subsides, gentle movement like walking or swimming helps prevent stiffness without overheating the joints.

patterns.symptoms: ["Pain and stiffness worse in cold, damp or windy weather", "Pain improves with warmth and gentle movement", "Joints feel cold to the touch, but not hot or red", "Heaviness and aching of the limbs", "Swelling without redness or heat", "Aversion to cold and wind"]

patterns.why_this_happens: When reactive arthritis follows a gut or urinary infection, the body's defenses are already weakened. If the lingering pathogen takes on a Cold-Damp nature, or if the person is constitutionally Yang-deficient, Cold and Dampness invade the channels and settle in the joints. This blocks the flow of Qi and Blood, causing stiffness, aching, and a distinctive cold sensation that eases with warmth.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale or slightly swollen body with a white greasy coating, moist surface. Pulse: moderate or tight, sometimes floating or soggy depending on whether Cold or Dampness dominates.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and Dampness are the main villains in this pattern - they congeal and obstruct the channels, making joints stiff and painful. Warmth, whether from a heating pad, warm food, or gentle motion, counteracts the cold and helps the body's Qi and Blood flow again. Dry weather and avoiding dampness prevent further accumulation of pathogenic Damp. Rest in a warm place allows the body to conserve Qi for recovery, while prolonged inactivity allows Dampness to settle and worsen the stagnation.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the affected joints warm and covered, especially in damp or windy weather. Eat warm, cooked foods like soups and stews with ginger, cinnamon and black pepper; avoid raw, cold or greasy foods that encourage internal Dampness. Gentle daily movement such as walking or tai chi helps keep the channels open without overstraining.

patterns.pattern_name: Dampness invading the Channels joints and muscles
patterns.symptoms: ["Heavy aching pain fixed in one place", "Joints feel swollen, heavy, and hard to move", "Numbness or loss of sensation in skin and muscles", "Worse in damp or rainy weather", "Poor appetite, bloating, and loose stools"]

patterns.better_with: Warm, dry weather, Gentle movement or stretching, Warm, cooked, nourishing foods, Rest and elevating the affected limb
patterns.why_this_happens:
After an infection, the body's defensive Qi is often weakened, allowing external Dampness to seep into the Channels and settle in the joints. Dampness is heavy, sticky, and Yin in nature, so it blocks the smooth flow of Qi and Blood, producing a deep, fixed ache and a sensation of heaviness in the limbs.
Because Dampness tends to sink and linger, the pain stays in one place and the joints become swollen and stiff, especially after rest. The Spleen is also affected, leading to poor appetite, bloating, and loose stools that further generate internal Dampness.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale or slightly swollen with teeth marks, coated with a thick, white, greasy fur that is excessively moist. Pulse: soggy (Ru) and often slow (Chi), with a slippery quality at the right Guan position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Dampness is a Yin pathogen that is heavy, sticky, and worsens with cold and moisture. Warm, dry weather and warm compresses help evaporate Dampness and unblock the Channels. Gentle movement encourages Qi and Blood to flow, which transforms Dampness and eases stiffness, while prolonged stillness allows Dampness to congeal and the pain to settle deeper. Warm, cooked foods support the Spleen's Yang, which is essential for transforming Dampness, whereas cold and greasy foods burden the Spleen and generate even more internal Dampness.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle:
Keep the joints warm and dry, especially in damp or rainy weather. Eat warm, cooked, easily digestible foods like soups, stews, and congees, and avoid cold, raw, and greasy items that create more Dampness.
Gentle daily movement such as walking or tai chi helps Qi circulate and transforms Dampness, but avoid overdoing it to the point of fatigue. Rest the affected limb when pain is acute, but do not stay completely still for long periods.

patterns.worse_with: Cold weather, Prolonged inactivity, Night time, Emotional stress, Cold or raw foods

patterns.why_this_happens: When reactive arthritis lingers, the persistent inflammation and dampness in the joints can obstruct the flow of Qi and Blood. Over time, this stagnation congeals into Blood Stasis, like a bruise deep in the tissues. The result is a fixed, stabbing pain that feels worse at night because blood circulation naturally slows during rest, and the stasis becomes more pronounced.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: dark purple body with stasis spots, thin white coat. Pulse: choppy (涩 sè) or wiry (弦 xián).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Blood Stasis obstructs the channels, causing fixed pain. Warmth and movement promote circulation, helping to break up stasis and ease pain. Cold and inactivity cause Blood to congeal, worsening the obstruction. Emotional stress stagnates Liver Qi, which in turn leads to more Blood Stasis, so calming the mind is essential.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat warming, blood-moving foods like turmeric, ginger, black pepper, and dark leafy greens. Avoid cold, raw foods and icy drinks that can congeal Blood. Gentle daily movement like walking or tai chi keeps Qi and Blood flowing; prolonged sitting or bed rest can worsen stagnation. Apply warm compresses to painful joints.

patterns.pattern_name: Painful Obstruction with Liver and Kidney Deficiency
patterns.symptoms: ["Dull, chronic joint ache", "Lower back and knee weakness", "Fatigue and pale complexion", "Worse with cold and damp weather", "Numbness or tingling in limbs"]
patterns.worse_with: Cold and damp weather, Overexertion or overwork, Cold or raw foods, Emotional stress
patterns.better_with: Warmth on the joints, Gentle movement or stretching, Rest, Warm, cooked, nourishing foods
patterns.why_this_happens: In TCM the Liver nourishes the sinews and the Kidneys govern the bones. When a reactive arthritis flare is not fully resolved, the lingering inflammation slowly depletes the body's reserves of Liver Blood and Kidney Essence. Over time the joints lose their lubrication and structural support, producing a dull, chronic ache that worsens with fatigue and cold, especially in the lower back and knees.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, thin body with a thin white coating. Pulse: fine, weak, and slow; the rear (Kidney) position is especially faint.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and damp weather further obstructs the already deficient channels, while warmth helps move Qi and Blood to ease pain. Overexertion depletes Qi and Blood, and raw cold foods introduce Cold and Damp, both of which worsen the underlying deficiency. Rest conserves the body's resources, and gentle movement keeps Qi flowing without draining reserves. Warm, nourishing foods directly supplement the Liver and Kidneys, and managing emotional stress protects the Spleen and Liver's role in producing Qi and Blood.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on warm, cooked foods that nourish the Kidneys and Liver, such as bone broths, black beans, walnuts, and goji berries. Avoid raw, cold, and greasy foods that can further weaken digestion and introduce Dampness. Keep the lower back and knees warm, especially in cold or damp weather, and incorporate gentle movement like Tai Chi or walking to maintain joint flexibility without overstraining.

patterns.why_this_happens: When reactive arthritis lingers or is treated with strong drying medications, the body's Qi and Yin can become depleted. Qi deficiency fails to nourish and support the joints, leading to persistent dull aches and overwhelming fatigue. Yin deficiency generates an empty heat that dries fluids, causing a dry mouth, night sweats, and a red, peeled tongue.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red or pale-red body with a thin or absent coating, possibly cracked and dry. Pulse: fine (thin) and weak, often rapid.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Rest conserves Qi, whereas overwork depletes it further. Nourishing, moistening foods replenish Yin fluids, while spicy and drying foods consume them. Gentle movement keeps Qi flowing without exhausting it, and avoiding excessive sweating prevents further loss of precious Yin fluids.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on gentle, nourishing foods like congee, steamed vegetables, and small amounts of lean protein. Avoid spicy, drying, and overly stimulating foods. Prioritize rest and avoid overexertion. Gentle exercises like Tai Chi or walking can help maintain Qi without depleting it.

It is commonly used for hot, swollen, painful joints with restricted movement, fever and chills, and a yellow greasy tongue coating. Often applied in conditions like gouty arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and other inflammatory joint diseases caused by the accumulation of dampness and heat in the body's meridian pathways.

It is commonly applied for hot, swollen, painful joints (especially in the knees and feet), lower limb weakness, and conditions like gout and eczema that involve a combination of inflammation and heavy, waterlogged tissue. The formula works by cooling inflammation, drying excess moisture, strengthening digestion to stop dampness at its source, and directing the formula's effects downward to the legs and lower body.

formulas.description: A classical formula used to relieve joint and muscle pain, stiffness, and numbness caused by Wind, Cold, and Dampness, especially when the body's own defensive and nourishing functions are weakened. It is particularly well suited for pain and tightness in the neck, shoulders, arms, and upper body that worsens in cold or damp weather.

formulas.translation: Aconite Decoction · Hàn dynasty, ~200 CE
formulas.properties: Hot, Warms the Channels and Disperses Cold, Dispels Dampness and Unblocks Painful Obstruction, Relieves pain in the joints and sinews
formulas.description: A classical formula for severe joint pain caused by cold and dampness lodged in the body. It powerfully warms the channels, disperses cold, and relieves pain in conditions where joints are stiff, aching, and worsened by cold weather. Due to the inclusion of Aconite root (a potent but toxic herb), this formula requires careful professional preparation and supervision.

formulas.translation: Notopterygium Decoction to Overcome Dampness · Jīn dynasty, ~1232 CE (published 1247 CE)
formulas.properties: Warm, Disperses Wind, Drains Dampness, Alleviates Pain
formulas.description: A classical formula for relieving body aches, stiffness, and heaviness caused by Wind and Dampness lodged in the muscles and joints. It is particularly suited for pain and stiffness in the head, neck, shoulders, back, and lower back that worsens in damp or windy weather. The formula works by using aromatic wind-dispersing herbs to gently push out the trapped Dampness through mild sweating.

formulas.description: A classical formula designed to improve blood circulation in the chest, relieve pain, and ease emotional tension. It is widely used for chronic chest pain, stubborn headaches, insomnia, and irritability caused by poor blood flow and stagnation in the upper body.

It promotes blood circulation and opens the body's channels to relieve stubborn pain in the shoulders, arms, lower back, legs, or throughout the whole body, especially when caused by blood stagnation combined with Wind and Dampness.

formulas.translation: Pubescent Angelica and Taxillus Decoction · Táng dynasty, 652 CE
formulas.properties: Warm, Dispels Wind-Dampness, Relieves Painful Obstruction, Supplements the Liver and Kidneys
formulas.description: A classical formula for chronic joint and lower back pain caused by long-term exposure to cold and dampness, combined with underlying weakness of the Liver, Kidneys, Qi, and Blood. It works on two fronts: expelling cold, wind, and dampness from the joints and sinews while also strengthening the body's constitution to prevent recurrence. It is especially suited for older adults or anyone whose pain has persisted for a long time and is accompanied by weakness, stiffness, or numbness in the lower body.

formulas.translation: Generate the Pulse Powder · Jīn dynasty, ~1186 CE
formulas.properties: Slightly Warm, Tonifies Qi, Generates Fluids, Nourishes Yin
formulas.description: A classical three-herb formula used to restore vitality when both Qi and body fluids have been depleted. It addresses fatigue, shortness of breath, excessive sweating, dry throat, and weak pulse caused by heat exhaustion, chronic illness, or prolonged coughing that has weakened the Lungs. In modern practice, it is also widely used as supportive treatment for heart conditions including heart failure and irregular heartbeat.

formulas.formula_name: Huang Qi Gui Zhi Wu Wu Tang
formulas.translation: Astragalus and Cinnamon Twig Five-Substance Decoction · Eastern Hàn dynasty, ~200 CE
formulas.properties: Warm, Tonifies Qi and warms the channels, Harmonizes the Nutritive and Defensive Qi, Nourishes Blood and dispels obstruction (Bi)
formulas.description: A classical formula used to improve circulation and relieve numbness, tingling, or weakness in the limbs caused by Qi deficiency and sluggish blood flow. It is especially suited for people who are prone to sweating, tire easily, and experience worsening symptoms in cold or windy conditions. Modern practitioners commonly apply it for peripheral neuropathy, post-stroke numbness, and Raynaud's phenomenon.

faqs.question: Can I use TCM alongside my NSAIDs or other arthritis medications?
faqs.answer: Yes, TCM can often be used alongside conventional medications, and many patients start herbs and acupuncture while still taking NSAIDs or DMARDs. However, some Chinese herbs that move Blood (like Dang Gui, Chuan Xiong, or Hong Hua) may increase the risk of bleeding when combined with blood thinners or high-dose NSAIDs. Always tell both your TCM practitioner and your prescribing doctor about everything you're taking so they can coordinate safely. Never stop prescribed medications abruptly without your doctor's guidance.

faqs.question: How many acupuncture sessions will I need?
faqs.answer: For an acute flare, weekly sessions are typical, with noticeable improvement often after 4-6 treatments. If your arthritis has become chronic, you may need 8-12 weekly sessions initially, then spacing them out to every other week or monthly as your condition stabilizes. Your practitioner will reassess your progress regularly and adjust the frequency. Acupuncture is just one part of the treatment - daily herbal medicine is equally important for lasting results.

faqs.question: Does TCM help prevent reactive arthritis from coming back?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's one of TCM's strengths. Once the acute inflammation is cleared, treatment shifts to strengthening your body's underlying weaknesses - whether that's building up Spleen Qi to prevent Dampness from accumulating again, or nourishing Liver and Kidney to support your joints long-term. Many people find that after a full course of TCM, they have fewer and milder recurrences, and some remain flare-free for years. Consistent diet and lifestyle adjustments play a big role in maintaining those results.

faqs.question: What foods should I avoid if I have reactive arthritis?
faqs.answer: In general, it's best to avoid foods that create Dampness and Heat in the body - greasy, fried, or heavily spiced dishes, excessive alcohol, and sugary foods. Dairy products and cold, raw foods can also worsen Dampness for many people. Instead, focus on warm, cooked meals with plenty of vegetables, whole grains, and moderate amounts of lean protein. Your specific pattern may require further adjustments - for example, if you have Damp-Heat, foods like barley and mung beans can be helpful, while Cold-Damp patterns benefit from warming spices like ginger and cinnamon. Your TCM practitioner will give you personalized guidance.

faqs.question: Is it safe to use Chinese herbs if I'm pregnant or breastfeeding?
faqs.answer: Some Chinese herbs are contraindicated during pregnancy, and others require careful dosing. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, always inform your TCM practitioner. They will select only herbs that are known to be safe for your situation and may rely more heavily on acupuncture and dietary therapy. Never self-prescribe herbal formulas during pregnancy. If you develop joint pain while pregnant, it's also important to see your medical doctor to rule out other conditions.

faqs.question: Will the acupuncture hurt?
faqs.answer: Acupuncture needles are extremely thin - much finer than a hypodermic needle - and most people feel only a brief, mild sensation when they are inserted, often described as a dull ache or tingling. Once the needles are in place, many patients feel deeply relaxed and may even fall asleep. If you're anxious about needles, let your practitioner know; they can use fewer points or gentler techniques to start.

faqs.question: Can TCM help if my reactive arthritis has already become chronic?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Chronic reactive arthritis often involves deeper deficiency patterns like Liver and Kidney Deficiency or Blood Stagnation. While these take longer to resolve, TCM's combination of herbs, acupuncture, and dietary therapy can gradually reduce pain, improve joint function, and boost your overall energy. Many people with long-standing arthritis find that TCM helps them reduce their reliance on pain medications and regain a better quality of life. Patience and consistency are key - expect treatment to last several months, with steady, gradual improvement.

research.title: Suppression of Inflammation by Si Miao San in Experimental Rheumatoid Arthritis Through Modulation of the AKT/ROS/Autophagy Axis
research.description: This animal study demonstrated that Si Miao San significantly reduced joint inflammation and synovial hyperplasia in a rat model of rheumatoid arthritis. The mechanism involved modulation of the AKT/ROS/autophagy pathway, providing a plausible molecular basis for its traditional use in damp-heat joint disorders like reactive arthritis.
